analysis:
I examined scripts/provider-release-publication.py, the new scripts/test-provider-cluster-runtime-models.py, and the pipeline-test changes in scripts/test-provider-release-pipeline.py. I found no concrete security regression in the supplied evidence.

Changed behavior: the release payload can now carry an optional cluster_runtime block (darkbloom_cluster_runtime_v2). load_cluster_runtime (lines 169-185) enforces a 64 KiB bound, rejects duplicate keys, and requires canonical JSON. check_cluster_runtime and its helpers (lines 71-145) enforce a closed field set and strict digest, model-ID, mode, cut and instant checks. check_cluster_derived_ids (161-166) bounds the derived approval IDs. validate() (215-222) runs these checks and the registration body size limit. prepare() reads the block before creating the folder, so a refused block leaves nothing behind.

The publish path re-validates the retained payload through checked_payload. That verifies the payload and provenance SHA-256 values, the source and run identity, and the immutable object URL. A cluster_runtime block therefore cannot be altered between the signing job and the publication job without failing the digest check. coordinator() still refuses redirects before sending the bearer RELEASE_KEY (A-005), and the registration body is sent over the configured COORDINATOR_URL.

The new test file covers a model-metadata fetcher whose implementation (scripts/provider-cluster-runtime-models.py) is not in the supplied units. Its tests assert no redirects, size caps, config.json size and digest checks against the manifest, a fixed User-Agent, and fail-without-writing behavior. The pipeline tests assert that the facts step runs after signing and notarization, uses no secrets, removes the signing keychain before running the app's CLI with `env -i`, and sends the block only when the *_CLUSTER_RUNTIME_ENABLED variable is true.

Not verified, so the next pass should check: the actual release-provider.yml step, scripts/provider-cluster-runtime-facts.sh, and provider-cluster-runtime-models.py; whether the CDN and coordinator manifests are trusted inputs to digests the coordinator treats as approval evidence; and the coordinator's handling of cluster_runtime (platform-owned, out of scope here). This PR does not alter the TB-011 or T-053 authorization boundaries as far as the supplied files show.
